title: Reranker lineage and budget-slicing for prefetch/rerank pipelines
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Non-chat rerank pipelines that do candidate-level calls (embeddings lookups, reranker scoring, or per-candidate function invocations for structured outputs) are currently producing inconsistent billing and quota accounting. Speculative prefetches and transient candidate evaluation paths lead to double-counting or uncancelled charges when a parent request aborts or when only a subset of candidates is returned. This ticket defines changes to attribute cost deterministically to the originating top-level request, enable budget slicing across candidates, and implement safe refunds/credits for cancelled speculative work.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Every top-level non-chat rerank request records a single canonical request id and candidate lineage that can be used to attribute tokens/units back to the parent.
2) Prefetch/speculative calls that are not materialized to the final response do not create irreversible charges; we either avoid billing them or emit a deterministic credit within 24 hours.
3) Quota checks are evaluated at the parent request boundary with an enforceable budget-slice model; child candidate evaluations consult the remaining slice before executing.
4) Billing reports and Data Warehouse dashboards show per-candidate cost rollup and reconcile to gross costs with <=0.1% variance over a week of traffic.
5) Rollout can be toggled per-customer via feature-flag and includes a shadow-billing mode for 2 weeks before full enforcement.
decision_log:
- Use a deterministic lineage header (X-Redwood-Parent-Id and X-Redwood-Candidate-Id) to tag work across services to avoid heuristic attribution.
- Implement parent-bounded quota checks: parent request gets 'budget_units'; child candidate evaluations acquire units via an optimistic linearized counter.
- For speculative prefetches we will: record speculative_mark=true and defer billing until a finalize signal from the parent; if not finalized within TTL, run an automated credit path.
- Avoid distributed two-phase commit: instead adopt idempotent event checkpoints and a compensation (credit) flow to handle refunds.
- Keep per-candidate accounting in the usage pipeline so reporting and quota enforcement have a single source of truth (billing kafka topic + DW ingestion).
tradeoffs:
- Pros: Deterministic attribution simplifies customer support and reduces overbilling incidents; avoids global transactions.
- Cons: Deferred billing and compensation increases complexity in billing pipeline and introduces latency before final cost is visible in invoices.
- Alternative considered: immediate best-effort charge with later reconciliations (rejected because of high noise and poor customer experience).
implementation_notes:
1) API changes: non-chat endpoints that call structured outputs or per-candidate functions will attach parent/candidate headers. Backwards compatible: fall back to existing behavior if headers missing.
2) Runtime: add budget-slicing module to serving runtime; new APIs: allocate_units(parent_id, candidate_id, units_requested) and finalize_candidate(parent_id,candidate_id,accepted:boolean).
3) Billing pipeline: consume new 'candidate_accounting' topic that emits per-candidate usage records with parent id and speculative flag; update metering processor to consider speculative=false for immediate invoicing.
4) Storage: store candidate checkpoints in existing usage-store bucket keyed by parent id for idempotency.
5) Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/lineage-budget-slicing (internal) ; Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 ; Billing pipeline PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/887 .
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal): unit tests + local integration with mock billing (2 days).
Phase 1 (shadow-billing): route 5% of production traffic through new attribution and write shadow records to candidate_accounting topic for 14 days; compare to current billing with reconciliation queries.
Phase 2 (opt-in): enable deterministic charging for a set of pilot customers with feature flag; monitor variance and support tickets.
Phase 3 (full enforcement): flip default to deterministic parent-charged billing; keep compensation flow enabled for 30 days.
Rollback: revert serving runtime feature flag; run compensation job to restore prior state if >0.5% of invoices require adjustment.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for header propagation, budget allocation logic, and idempotent finalize flow.
- Integration tests: simulate parent abort with partially completed candidate evaluations; assert that speculative calls are not invoiced.
- Stress test: 10k req/s synthetic workload with multi-candidate fanout to validate allocation contention.
- End-to-end staging: shadow-billing run and compare aggregate costs to current pipeline with drift <0.1%.
- QA checklist: confirm DW exports, Grafana dashboards, and customer invoices reflect expected rows.
